note: OWNER BLOCKERS — Eitan's rule, 2026-08-10: 'If there is something critical to the project that I absolutely must do, regardless of what I say, do not continue working until I have finished that task.' A blocker here HALTS feature work on BOTH loops (interactive and away). It is deliberately hard to add: only a task that (a) ONLY Eitan can do, and (b) blocks the current milestone, qualifies. Repair of something the loop itself broke is NEVER a blocker — that is the loop's own debt to pay.

rules.who_clears: Eitan only. Claude may propose a blocker; only Eitan sets status to 'done'.
rules.what_continues_while_blocked: Nothing that advances the milestone. Safety fixes, honest reporting, and preparing the material Eitan needs to decide are allowed — they serve the unblock.
rules.abuse_guard: If Claude cannot name what SPECIFICALLY unblocks and why no default is safe, it is not a blocker — it is Claude avoiding a decision that is its own to make.

blockers.title: Define what makes an element GOOD — the quality bar
blockers.why_only_eitan: This is taste, and it is the owner's product. The last two times Claude set a bar itself, the result was 14 fabricated template packs and a guardrail that never ran. A bar Claude invents is the bar that already failed twice.
why_it_blocks: CREATORS is wired to a real model but gate G3 holds it closed — with no bar, it can publish nothing, so the department is inert.
9,435 of 11,278 elements (83.7%) have pattern-matched text. Whether re-analysis is worth running, and what it should produce, depends entirely on what 'good' means.
M1 is 'usable hub'. Usable by whose standard is the unanswered part of the milestone.
blockers.what_unblocks_it: Eitan judges a handful of REAL elements from his own hub and says which are keepers and which are junk, and why. Claude turns that into the written bar and a test. He does not need to author a spec.

blockers.title: Refresh the dead model IDs — 11 of 12 engines are down, so every agent is one small model
blockers.why_only_eitan: Fixing this means reading OpenRouter's CURRENT free-model list and pasting the real IDs. This session has no web egress, and Claude's training knowledge is stale for exactly the models the plan targets (GLM-5.2 / DeepSeek V4 / Qwen 3.6 / Kimi K2.7 are all NEWER than the IDs configured). Guessing an ID produces another 404 and another week of one-model output.

evidence.room_reality: 160 committed room turns: mistral 85.6%, nvidia 13.8%, groq 0.6%. Zero GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen or Kimi have EVER spoken.

why_it_blocks: The multi-brain premise is the core of the architecture and it is currently fiction: 85.6% of all agent turns ran on mistral-small-latest, a SMALL model.
PROTOCOLS bans same-model-different-prompt as correlated errors. That is precisely what is running today, so every 'debate' is one small model arguing with itself.
This is the actual cause of the carbon-copy output Eitan saw -- not only the f-string templates.
blockers.what_unblocks_it: Open openrouter.ai/models, filter to free, and paste back the current IDs for a GLM, a DeepSeek, a Qwen and a Kimi model. Claude updates CATALOG and reruns engine_selftest. If OmniRoute is preferred instead, set OMNIROUTE_KEY and it becomes the gateway -- but note the problem is NOT quota shortage, it is dead IDs, so OmniRoute alone would not fix it.
blockers.claude_correction: Claude first told Eitan this was 'one missing key'. That was wrong: a 404 means the request was made and answered, so the key is live. Corrected within the same fire.
